data.name: Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30™
data.detailed_description:
Baseado numa história real. Situada durante o famoso lançamento aéreo antes da invasão à Normandia, onde o Sgt. Matt Baker e o seu esquadrão de 101 pára-quedistas se espalharam pelo interior da França.
À medida que a história se desenvolve, terás de escolher entre o sucesso da tua missão e a vida dos teus homens - os teus irmãos de armas.
Brothers In Arms: Road to Hill 30 imerge jogadores na histórica invasão de oito dias à Normandia - com imagens inigualáveis, autenticidade, som, e jogabilidade.
Único: Brothers In Arms Road to Hill 30 é o único jogo de tiro em primeira pessoa tático situado na Segunda Guerra Mundial.
Táticas militares reais: Controles de esquadrão intuitivos e fáceis de usar apelam tanto a jogadores experientes como a novatos.
Soldados reais: Com um elenco de mais de 20 personagens, cada uma com personalidade, aparência e estilo únicos.
Inteligência artificial revolucionária: Aliados e inimigos usam os procedimentos normais de disparo e manobração para flanquear e matar os seus oponentes.
Autenticidade sem precedentes: Campos de batalha, eventos e equipamento detalhados e historicamente precisos, recriados a partir de fotografias da Army Signal Corps, de imagens aéreas, e de relatos de testemunhas oculares.
Multijogador inovador: Os jogadores comandam equipas de 3 homens controlados por inteligência artificial, numa batalha de inteligência e habilidade, para cumprir objetivos emocionantes.
Equipa premiada: Gearbox Software, criadores de Half-Life Oppossing Force e desenvolvedores de James Bond: Nightfire, Counter-Strike, e Halo (PC).

content_descriptors.notes:
Based on a true story. Set during the famous airdrop before the invasion at Normandy, where Sgt. Matt Baker and his squad of 101st Airborne Paratroopers were scattered over the French countryside. 
As the story unfolds, you must choose between the success of your mission and the lives of your men - your brothers in arms.

reviews.review:
My first time knowing about the existance of this series was playing Brothers in Arms 2: Global Front on my first smartphone back when I was a teen. More than a decade later, I finally experience the series proper, starting with Road to Hill 30.

I got to say, this game was a breath of fresh air than the standard WW2 FPS titles from COD and MOH. Like many had point out, it's a squad based tactical FPS than requires using some planning to progress rather than just going ham using brute force. As Sergeant Matt Baker, you take part in the Normandy Campaign completing missions by leading a squad of 2 teams (each for the majority consisting of 3 bros). The teams you are given are a gun team and an assault team for the most part. In some missions, you will get a tank (or two) as part of your squad to command.

As mentioned, the game is tactical...kind of like a mini RTS but you are on ground doing the commanding. You get to direct your bros to take cover, lay covering fire, close in to assault an enemy position or follow you around. How you use them is by observing the map for opportunities, which you can toggle to get a bird's eye view from your position or you can cycle to the views on your teams, enemy, or the checkpoint positions to get a general layout to plan your move. I admit the I rarely use the map view cause the navigation can be a bit wonky. Also unlike COD, your bros are VALUABLE and are your lifeline, it's best to keep most of them alive when progressing toward the end of the mission. Them dying (don't worry they will come back next mission unless scripted to die) early will actually make things difficult. I am often forced to manually do checkpoint restarts most of the time when that happens.

The bread and butter tactic for most of the campaign is usually straightforward, let the bros give covering fire to pin enemies down while you go or position another team to flank the pinned enemies. Speaking of pinning enemies with covering fire, I like the system where there will be a circle on an enemy team showing their status via three colours When the circle is red, they are a threat and free to shoot you, so suppressing them by firing will cause the circle to progressively turn grey like a clock. When it is grey, they are pinned and are forced into cover (also making it harder to kill them face on), that's where the flanking opportunity can be seized to take them out. Once you get the general idea, completing objectives is really fun. Though the sudden difficulty spike at the [spoiler] clearing the warehouse part in the Push into Carentan mission [/spoiler] was not me finest hour.

However, I have one gripe, the gunplay. Oh boy, it's absolutely terrible. I feel like I am a stormtrooper shooting each time I click the left mouse button. The recoil is so high you will miss most of your shots. Aiming down sight is like using a sniper rifle in COD, where your breathing causes the aim to keep swaying which means you will ALSO miss most of your shots...and you can't hold it. Enemies can be also quite spongy, from what I feel like, which make things worse. I get that they are going for realism but man, even at point blank close range you still can miss shots, that sucks man. But don't let me pointing this out deter you from getting this game, it's still a great and fun game. 

As for the story, I like it. It's pretty grounded in reality where Sergeant Matt Baker just a guy overwhelmed by the heavy responsibility of keeping his men alive in this hellish war. And oh boy you will tragically lose some bros permanently in the story. For the most part, I find it funny how he is a silent protag like COD protags in mission cutscenes yet is able to shout commands in gameplay [spoiler] until the ending...where we also finally get to see his face [/spoiler]. He also fully speaks when giving the opening narration for each mission that are sometimes existential and depressing. Another praise from me is that this game really make you remember who are the bros in your squad as well as the commanding officers. I like how is a nice change from the one man army and epic cinematics I am used to. I look forward on how the story progresses in the next 2 games.

I give Brothers in Arms: Road to Hill 30 a recommended an 8/10, one of the must haves for WW2 buffs. Would have been higher if the gunplay was not a stormtrooper simulator.
